tasks.subject: When a parse action returns a non-ParseResults, non-list value (e.g. a tuple, set, or defaultdict), the named result was being set to only the first element (tokens[0]) instead of the full return value. This happened because the value was passed directly to ParseResults(), which indexes into it with 'toklist[0]' for the named result.
tasks.body:
Fix: wrap non-list, non-ParseResults return values in [tokens]
before constructing the ParseResults, so toklist[0] returns the
full value. Null values (empty tuple) are not wrapped because
ParseResults._null_values expects them directly to clear the
result. Lists preserve their existing behavior of spreading
elements as the token list.

Partially fixes #401

tasks.subject: Fix RecursionError for bounded repetition with large upper bound (issue #332) (#652)
tasks.body:
* Fix RecursionError for bounded repetition with large upper bound (issue #332)

Build the optional tail of `expr * (m, n)` as a flat list of independent
`Optional` expressions instead of a deeply nested `Optional(self + ...)`
chain. The nested form recursed `optElements` levels deep, raising
RecursionError for large upper bounds such as `expr[..., 1000]`.

Fixes #332.

* Preserve early-exit in bounded repetition (issue #332)

Replace the flat And([Opt(self)] * optElements) tail with a bounded
ZeroOrMore(self, max=optElements). The flat list always attempted self for
every remaining slot in the upper bound, losing the original recursive
form's early-exit behavior (ptmcg's review on PR #652). The bounded loop
is flat (no RecursionError at large upper bounds) and still stops at the
first non-match, so construction, parsing, and early-exit all hold.

- Add optional max bound to _MultipleMatch/ZeroOrMore
- Add testBoundedRepetitionLargeUpperBoundEarlyExit regression test

* Added validation for max parameter, must be > 0; added unit tests for added max parameter

tasks.subject: Fix Dict returning an empty nested ParseResults.as_dict() as [] instead of {}; remove vestigial ParseResults._modal attribute; fix incidental bug when Dict tries to create a dict with a ParseResults value for a key (not hashable); incorporated partial solution submitted in PR #635
Preserve whitespace in QuotedString multi-char delimiters (fixes #492)
tasks.body:
QuotedString.__init__ called quote_char.strip() (and end_quote_char.strip())
to reject empty/whitespace-only delimiters. But strip() also removed leading
or trailing whitespace that is a legitimate part of a multi-character
delimiter. For example QuotedString("\n;", multiline=True) had its quote_char
silently collapsed to ";", so the newline in the delimiter was ignored and
matching started/ended at the wrong positions.

Fix: validate with `not quote_char.strip()` to keep rejecting empty or
all-whitespace delimiters, but assign the original, unstripped value so
embedded whitespace in a valid delimiter is preserved. Same for end_quote_char.

Added a regression test covering the reported cases and confirming that empty
and all-whitespace quote chars are still rejected.

tasks.subject: fix: deepcopy results names referencing nested ParseResults
tasks.body:
ParseResults.deepcopy() only deep-copied the token list; the results-name
dict (_tokdict) still referenced the original tokens. So a named token that
was also a list item became inconsistent after the copy: reaching it by name
returned the original object while reaching it by index returned the copy, and
mutating either the original or the copy was visible through the other by name.

Rebuild _tokdict during deepcopy so that names point at the deep-copied tokens,
keeping the copy internally consistent and fully decoupled from the original.

tasks.subject: fix: as_datetime passes ParseResults instead of input string to ParseException
tasks.body:
as_datetime() raised ParseException(t, l, msg) with the parse
results 't' as the pstr argument, which should be the input string
's'.  This caused a secondary TypeError when the exception message
was formatted, because pstr is expected to be a string for line/col
computation.

Other parse actions in the same class (convert_to_date,
convert_to_datetime) correctly use the input string argument, so
this was a one-character oversight.

tasks.subject: fix: ParseResults.__add__ and __radd__ arithmetic contract violations
tasks.body:
- __add__: add isinstance guard, return NotImplemented instead of
  crashing with AttributeError on non-ParseResults operands
- __radd__: return NotImplemented instead of other + self for
  non-zero operands, preventing infinite RecursionError
- 0 + ParseResults (sum() builtin) preserved

tasks.subject: Fix as_datetime mis-scaling fractional seconds into microsecond field
tasks.body:
pyparsing_common.as_datetime scaled the fractional part of the seconds
field by 1000 (milliseconds) and floor-truncated it, then stored the
result in the datetime microsecond field. Parsing "1997-07-16T19:20:30.45"
yielded microsecond=449 instead of 450000, disagreeing with the sibling
convert_to_datetime parse action and the standard library.

Scale the fraction to microseconds with round() to also avoid the
floating-point floor error (0.45 * 1e6 == 449999.99...).

tasks.subject: Fix Located capturing leading whitespace in its location (#621)
tasks.body:
Located adopts callPreparse from the wrapped expression. When that
expression delegates whitespace skipping to its sub-expressions (such as
MatchFirst or And, whose callPreparse is False), Located does not
pre-parse it, so parseImpl captured start on the leading whitespace and
locn_start (and the located span) wrongly included that whitespace.

Capture start after the wrapped expression's own preParse, so locn_start
marks the real start of the match. Expressions modified with
leave_whitespace() still keep their leading whitespace.

Adds a regression test and a CHANGES entry.
